items.title: α-tocopherol (Vitamin E) inhibits second mitochondria-derived activator of caspases (SMAC) mimetic-induced cell death by directly targeting cIAP1 degradation.
items.abstract: Tocopherols (vitamin E) are well characterized as essential lipophilic antioxidant agents. However, recent evidence suggests that tocopherols may also regulate cellular signalling through direct interactions with specific protein targets. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanism by which α-tocopherol regulates programmed cell death and to identify its direct molecular target. A high-throughput screen identified α-tocopherol as an inhibitor of TNF-α/SMAC-mimetic-induced cell death. The mechanism(s) underlying this action of α-tocopherol was investigated using western blotting, immunoprecipitation, ubiquitination assays, drug affinity responsive target stability, cellular thermal shift assay, isothermal titration calorimetry and molecular docking. Its efficacy, in vivo, was evaluated in a murine model of ulcerative colitis, induced by dextran sulphate sodium (DSS). α-Tocopherol selectively inhibited TNF-α/SMAC-mimetic-induced cell death by directly and competitively binding to the BIR3 domain of the inhibitor of apoptosis protein-1 (cIAP1). This interaction stabilized cIAP1, prevented the formation of RIPK1-dependent death complexes and suppressed apoptosis and necroptosis. In a murine model of DSS-induced colitis, α-tocopherol significantly alleviated disease severity while preserving cIAP1 protein expression. Our findings identified cIAP1 as a previously unrecognized molecular target of α-tocopherol and demonstrated that cIAP1 stabilization contributed to the suppression of RIPK1-dependent cell death. These findings expand the current understanding of the biological functions of tocopherols and provide a mechanistic basis for their potential therapeutic application in inflammatory diseases associated with aberrant cIAP1 degradation.

items.title: Association Between Cachexia, Defined Using the Asian Working Group for Cachexia 2023 Criteria, and Exercise Capacity in Patients Undergoing Haemodialysis.
items.abstract: Patients undergoing haemodialysis (HD) are at high risk of developing cachexia. Early detection and implementation of interventions are essential. However, associations between cachexia and exercise capacity in patients undergoing HD remain unclear. We examined the associations between cachexia and exercise capacity in HD patients. This cross-sectional study included outpatients on maintenance HD who underwent the cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) and physical function assessments. Cachexia was defined based on the Asian Working Group for Cachexia (AWGC) 2023 criteria. Pre-cachexia was diagnosed in patients who did not meet the definition of cachexia but fulfilled at least one mandatory or optional criterion. Pre-cachexia was operationally classified by the authors based on the AWGC 2023 criteria. Assessments of exercise capacity included peak oxygen uptake (peak VO 2 ), peak work rate (peak WR) and ventilatory equivalent for carbon dioxide (VE/VCO 2 ) slope, measured using the CPET. Exercise capacity was compared across cachexia stages. 109 patients (median age: 70.0 years; female: 28.4%) were included, with 21.1%, 45.9% and 33.0% classified as non-cachexia, pre-cachexia and cachexia, respectively. Patients with cachexia were older, had a higher VE/VCO 2 slope, and lower peak WR than those without cachexia. Patients with pre-cachexia also showed a lower peak WR than those without cachexia. Peak VO 2 was not significantly associated with cachexia stage. In outpatients on maintenance HD, cachexia was associated with reduced exercise capacity. Furthermore, lower muscle function was observed in the pre-cachexia and cachexia.

items.title: Current Status and Outcomes of Infective Endocarditis in Adults With Congenital Heart Disease in Japan　- A Nationwide JROAD-DPC Analysis.
items.abstract: Nationwide data on infective endocarditis (IE) in adults with congenital heart disease (ACHD) in Japan are limited. Using a nationwide Japanese administrative database (2013-2023), we identified 822 ACHD patients (median age 41 years; 32.0% female) hospitalized for IE. In-hospital mortality rate was 4.0%, and cardiac surgery was performed in 38.6%. Older age, severe CHD complexity, and pulmonary hypertension were independently associated with in-hospital death. This study clarified the clinical characteristics and outcomes of IE in ACHD in Japan.
items.journal: Circulation journal : official journal of the Japanese Circulation Society

items.title: Impact of the Safety-Net Kidney-After-Heart Transplant Policy on Simultaneous Heart-Kidney Transplant Volume and Outcomes in the United States.
items.abstract: On 6/29/2023, the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) implemented a safety-net policy providing priority kidney transplant (KT) listing status to heart transplant (HT) recipients who develop persistent kidney dysfunction within one year of HT, with the intent of incentivizing isolated HT over simultaneous heart-kidney transplantation (sHKT) in patients with potentially reversible kidney dysfunction. The impact of this policy on sHKT utilization and post-transplant outcomes is unknown. We used interrupted time series analysis of quarterly sHKT volume and compared one-year mortality and kidney graft failure between pre- and post-policy sHKT recipients using multivariable Cox models. In this OPTN registry analysis of HTs performed from 1/1/2020-12/31/2025, among 21,688 HT recipients, 1,133 pre-policy and 877 post-policy recipients underwent sHKT, and 183 received a safety-net KT. We found that 1) following policy implementation, the quarterly change in slope of sHKT utilization was -4.45 procedures per quarter (95% CI -5.94, -2.95), with a concurrent rise in safety-net KT of 2.52 per quarter (95% CI 1.44, 3.59), 2) mortality and kidney graft failure were similar among sHKT recipients post- vs pre-policy implementation (hazard ratio [HR] 0.94, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.68, 1.29 and HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.67, 1.24, respectively).
items.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons

items.title: Identifying Structural Heart Disease and Prioritizing Echocardiography Through Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Tele-ECG: An External Validation of the PROVAR+ Study.
items.abstract: Structural heart disease (SHD) is underdiagnosed where echocardiography access is limited. We evaluated the role of artificial intelligence-enabled ECG for SHD detection (AI-ECG-SHD) in cardiovascular screening. We prospectively enrolled adults undergoing public-system cardiovascular screening in two Brazilian cities. Participants underwent clinical assessment, digital 12-lead tele-ECG, and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) interpreted by cardiologists. ECG signals were analyzed using a validated AI-ECG-SHD algorithm through an application programming interface. SHD was defined as moderate/severe ventricular dysfunction/hypertrophy, wall-motion abnormalities, moderate/severe valvular disease, congenital heart disease, or pericardial disease. AI-ECG-SHD performance was assessed at a predefined threshold and discrimination compared with a model incorporating clinical variables and major conventional ECG abnormalities. Number needed to screen (NNS) was calculated. Among 3,779 participants (median age 66 years; 56.7% women), 58.7% screened AI-ECG-SHD-positive and 24.2% had TTE-detected SHD. Major ECG abnormalities (OR=3.73), age (OR=1.22/10-years), male sex (OR=1.50), Chagas disease (OR=1.89), coronary disease (OR=3.01), and heart failure (OR=1.33) independently predicted SHD. AI-ECG-SHD probability (each 10% increase) was strongly associated with SHD (OR 1.55, 95%CI 1.51-1.61; p<0.001) and showed superior discrimination versus the conventional model (AUC 0.80, 95%CI 0.78-0.82 vs 0.75, 95%CI 0.74-0.77; p<0.001). AI-ECG-SHD achieved 59.4% accuracy, 87.3% sensitivity, 50.4% specificity, 92.6% negative-predictive value, diagnostic odds ratio 7.00, and NNS 4.7. AI-guided prioritization reduced estimated time to diagnosis of 50% of SHD cases from 407 to 172 days under fixed TTE capacity. In conclusion, AI-ECG-SHD improved SHD detection over conventional prediction and may enable scalable, resource-efficient TTE prioritization in underserved public healthcare systems.

items.title: Effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against laboratory-confirmed influenza among older adults in Eastern China: A test-negative case-control study.
items.abstract: Evidence on the real-world effectiveness of seasonal influenza vaccination among older adults in China remains limited and varies by season and circulating virus. We used a test-negative case-control design to estimate the effectiveness of the 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine against medically attended, laboratory-confirmed influenza among adults aged ≥60 years attending two sentinel hospitals in Shengzhou, Zhejiang Province. Participants vaccinated ≥14 days before symptom onset were considered vaccinated; those vaccinated 0-13 days before onset were excluded from the primary analysis. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was calculated as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100% using multivariable logistic regression. Among 532 participants in the primary analysis, 156 were influenza-positive cases and 376 were test-negative controls. Effective current-season vaccination was recorded in 32.7% of cases and 48.4% of controls. Adjusted VE against any influenza was 46% (95% confidence interval [CI], 18-64). Type-specific VE was 42% (95% CI, 8-63) against influenza A and 60% (95% CI, 14-81) against influenza B. Subtype-specific estimates were less precise, and interaction analyses did not identify differences by age group or chronic-disease status. The overall estimate remained stable across diagnostic restrictions and alternative model specifications. The 2025-2026 trivalent influenza vaccine was associated with moderate protection against medically attended influenza in older adults under routine program conditions, supporting continued seasonal vaccination and multi-season surveillance.

items.title: A Two-Stage Strategy to Reprogram Cyanine Photosensitizers as Controllable-Pyroptosis Inducers for Anticancer Phototherapy.
items.abstract: Pyroptosis, a lytic and inflammatory form of programmed cell death, provides a promising strategy for antitumor immunotherapy. However, controllable modulation of pyroptosis using phototherapeutic agents remains challenging. In this study, we report a two-stage molecular reprogramming method to rationally design cyanine photosensitizers with tunable pyroptosis-inducing activity. We first reprogram IR808 into a novel photosensitizer T808, by integrating a tetraphenylethylene unit with IR808, which consequently enhances excited - state features related to intersystem crossing (ISC) and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation capability, accompanied by inducing pyroptosis under irradiation. In the second process, T808 is conjugated with poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) chains of varying lengths (M.W. 550, 1000, and 2000 Da) to finely modulate the pyroptotic efficacy. The relationship of PEG chain length with pyroptosis-inducing activity is in the order of PT550 > T808 > PT1000 >> PT2000. Cellular and in vivo studies show that T808, PT550, and PT1000 treatments suppress tumor growth and induce pyroptosis with occurrence of immunogenic cell death (ICD). Even under a lower intratumoral injection dose (25 µM), T808 and PT550 therapies exhibit remarkable antitumor efficacy with measurable pyroptosis features. This work provides a new insight into reprogramming cyanine photosensitizers into pyroptosis-active molecules, and proposes possible structural association of PEGylated cyanines with the pyroptosis activity.

items.title: Individualizing Apheresis Processing Volumes Using a Predictive Algorithm: Analysis of the CAR T-Cell Collection Protocol Utilized in ACIT001/EXC002, a Phase Ib/II Trial of Decentralized Production of CAR T Cells for Treatment of Relapsed/Refractory Aggressive NHL and ALL.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has become an established treatment for relapsed or refractory B-cell malignancies. Apheresis collection of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) is a critical first step in CAR T-cell manufacturing. However, the total blood volume (TBV) required to achieve adequate T-cell yield is difficult to predict. As a result, standard practice often involves processing two to four TBVs, which may lead to unnecessary time on machine (TOM) and increased risk of procedure-related complications such as citrate toxicity, hypovolemia, and thrombocytopenia. As part of the ACIT001/EXC002 clinical trial evaluating point-of-care CAR T-cell manufacturing for relapsed/refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) or acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), we developed a pragmatic protocol to individualize TBV processing. This protocol uses a preliminary TBV estimate based on an assumed CD3-positive T-cell collection efficiency (CE) of 50%, followed by a midpoint product assessment to measure actual CE and adjust the remaining TBV and TOM. Using this approach, the preliminary estimate was adequate or conservative in 72% of procedures, and over 75% of patients required less than the standard two to four TBVs. The target CD3-positive T-cell yield was achieved in 93% of patients. These findings demonstrate that a midpoint-adjusted TBV calculation protocol can minimize unnecessary TOM while maintaining reliable T-cell collection, thereby improving resource utilization and patient safety. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03938987.

items.title: [Advances and current status of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in older adults: expanding indications and challenges in clinical practice].
items.abstract: With the rapid aging of Japan's population, the proportion of older patients with hematologic malignancies has increased, and the eligible age range for allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) has expanded accordingly. With advances in conditioning regimens, novel agents, supportive care, and post-transplant management, HSCT is now a realistic therapeutic option even for carefully selected patients over 70 years of age. Nevertheless, older adults are a highly heterogeneous population, and chronological age alone is no longer sufficient for transplant decision-making. This review summarizes recent international and Japanese registry data on outcomes of HSCT in older patients and presents real-world results of cord blood transplantation in patients aged 65 years and older at the author's institution. It highlights the roles of comorbidity assessment using the HCT-CI, geriatric assessment, and frailty evaluation in refining transplant eligibility and predicting non-relapse mortality (NRM). Strategies to reduce NRM-including individualized conditioning selection, prehabilitation interventions, multidisciplinary supportive care, and discharge planning-are also discussed. Collectively, current evidence suggests that the approach to transplantation in older adults is shifting from simply expanding the eligible age range toward optimizing transplant quality and patient-centered outcomes.
items.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology

items.title: [Treatment strategies for lymphoma in older adults].
items.abstract: As the Japanese population continues to age, the proportion of older adults with malignant lymphoma is also increasing. Because older adults exhibit considerable interindividual variability due to reduced functional reserve, comorbidities, and malnutrition, they face a greater risk of infections and other serious adverse events than younger patients. Therefore, multifaceted assessments such as comprehensive geriatric assessment are important in treatment selection. For diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), standard-dose R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP is recommended for patients under 80 years old, whereas dose-reduced regimens or individualized treatments are considered for those 80 years and older or frail patients. Since follicular lymphoma (FL) is not considered curable, it is crucial to set more individualized treatment goals and select treatments accordingly. Advances in non-cytotoxic novel drugs and supportive therapies, particularly cellular immunotherapies, are expanding treatment opportunities even for older adults. However, challenges remain due to insufficient clinical trial data and the lack of established optimal treatment methods. Treatment strategies that consider the unique background of older adults are needed.
items.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology

items.title: Rat hepatitis E virus RNA detection in isolated cases of acute undifferentiated febrile illness without acute hepatitis.
items.abstract: Rat hepatitis E virus (ratHEV; Rocahepevirus ratti) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen whose clinical spectrum is predominantly hepatic. Whether ratHEV causes acute undifferentiated febrile illness (AUFI) without acute hepatitis has not been systematically evaluated. This retrospective observational study at a southern Spain tertiary hospital (April 2021-October 2023) evaluated patients tested for Rickettsia spp. and/or Coxiella burnetii. AUFI was defined as community-acquired fever ≥38°C lasting <21 days without localizing features or initial etiology; patients with acute hepatitis were excluded. AUFI cases were compared with contemporaneous febrile patients presenting with a localizing focus. The primary outcome was sequence-confirmed infection. Detections without sequence recovery were classified as probable infections. Of 1,684 patients assessed, 312 were eligible: 81 with AUFI (median age 53 years [IQR, 37-64]; 54 [66.7%] men) and 231 comparators. Sequence-confirmed ratHEV infection occurred in 1/81 AUFI patients (1.2%; 95% CI, 0.2-6.7) and 0/231 comparators (0%; 95% CI, 0-1.6; P = 0.260). Two additional AUFI patients had detectable ratHEV RNA without sequence recovery. Combining confirmed and probable infections, ratHEV RNA was detected in 3/81 AUFI patients (3.7%; 95% CI, 1.3-10.3; P = 0.017). The confirmed infection presented as a self-limiting febrile illness without liver dysfunction, ratHEV RNA cleared upon fever resolution. The recovered genotype C1 sequence clustered with ratHEV rodent sequences from the same region. RatHEV RNA was detected exclusively among AUFI patients. These findings support prospectively evaluating ratHEV as a potential cause of AUFI where the virus circulates in animal reservoirs.
items.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

items.title: Antiretroviral therapy, adiposity, and cardiometabolic risk in people with HIV.
items.abstract: Return to health accounts for only part of the weight gain observed with modern antiretroviral therapy (ART). A fuller account requires integrating recovery from HIV-related catabolism, HIV-associated adipose tissue remodelling, withdrawal of weight-suppressive antiretrovirals, possible direct or permissive effects of newer agents, individual susceptibility, and obesogenic environments. Evidence from ART initiation and switch studies, PrEP trials, and mechanistic research in adipose tissue suggests that ART-associated weight gain is heterogeneous rather than a uniform restorative process. Once adiposity is established, ART switching has a limited ability to reverse weight gain, consistent with the biological persistence of acquired adiposity. Future care should move beyond ART manipulation alone and incorporate early monitoring, body-composition assessment, cardiometabolic prevention, lifestyle intervention, and appropriate antiobesity pharmacotherapy.

items.title: Ectasia to Ecstatic: A Case Report of Immunoglobulin G4-Related Disease Masquerading as Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
items.abstract: Immunoglobulin G4-sclerosing cholangitis (IgG4-SC) is a rare fibroinflammatory disease that involves the biliary duct and can often mimic primary sclerosing cholangitis. It is a chronic disease that has the potential to progress to cirrhosis if left untreated. Obtaining a biopsy and serum IgG levels are crucial for diagnosis and understanding the extent of the disease. Here, we present a case of IgG4-SC in a woman with no prior biliary history, who initially presented with mid-abdominal pain and jaundice. She underwent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, which demonstrated a distal biliary stricture requiring stenting, although imaging demonstrated concern for autoimmune cholangitis given the diffuse ectasia seen. Serum IgG4 levels were found to be four times the upper limit of normal and liver biopsy was consistent with IgG4-related disease, so the patient was started on glucocorticoids with a positive response. IgG4-SC can be a difficult diagnosis to obtain and often mimics other pathologies, so it is an important diagnostic consideration given that it can typically be treated within the correct clinical context.

items.title: Diagnostic challenge of delayed immune-related hepatitis during zongertinib treatment after nivolumab plus ipilimumab in a 52-year-old man with HER2-mutant non-small cell lung cancer: a case report.
items.abstract: Delayed immune-related hepatitis after discontinuation of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is increasingly recognized, but attribution is difficult when liver injury develops during subsequent tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) therapy. This diagnostic dilemma has not been well described during human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-selective TKI treatment after dual ICI therapy. A 52-year-old Japanese man with HER2 exon 20 insertion-positive stage IVB non-small cell lung cancer received nivolumab plus ipilimumab from February 28 to November 13, 2025, and developed grade 2 oral mucositis, grade 2 adrenal insufficiency, and grade 1-2 skin toxicity. Zongertinib was initiated on November 26. Routine testing on January 6, 2026 showed grade 3 hepatocellular injury, and zongertinib was withheld. Despite drug withdrawal, liver injury progressed, and he was admitted with mild fatigue on January 20, when aspartate aminotransferase, alanine aminotransferase, alkaline phosphatase, and γ-glutamyl transpeptidase levels were 774, 1,386, 156, and 160 U/L, respectively. Total bilirubin remained approximately 1.0 mg/dL. Viral and autoimmune testing and imaging disclosed no alternative cause. Liver biopsy showed active hepatitis with lymphocyte-predominant portal and lobular inflammation and interface activity, findings compatible with an immune-mediated hepatitis pattern but not specific for the causative agent. Prednisolone 40 mg/day (approximately 0.5 mg/kg/day) produced rapid biochemical improvement with resolution of fatigue. Zongertinib was resumed on February 11 and continued without recurrent hepatitis through June 2026. The progression of liver injury despite zongertinib withdrawal, multiple prior immune-related adverse events, exclusion of competing causes, compatible histology, corticosteroid responsiveness, and absence of recurrence after zongertinib rechallenge collectively favored delayed immune-related hepatitis, although zongertinib-associated drug-induced liver injury could not be completely excluded. In similar cases, a structured etiological assessment, including liver biopsy when the result may alter cancer treatment, can help guide management.

items.title: Health-care burden of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease in European tertiary-care outpatient clinics (CONSTANS): a prospective multicentre cohort study.
items.abstract: Despite modeling-based epidemiological studies of MASLD, precise estimates of the prevalence and health-care resource utilization in outpatient clinical practice are unknown. We assessed, in a real-life setting, the prevalence of suspected/confirmed MASLD and described health-care resource utilization. A prospective, observational study of patients attending the outpatient hepato-gastroenterology clinics of eight European tertiary care centers during three months. Follow-up data of patients with suspected/confirmed MASLD were recorded 12 months after the screening visit: final diagnosis, disease stage, diagnostic work-up and the use of health-care resources. 5240 outpatients from Germany, France, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Italy, Spain and Slovakia were screened. The main reasons for visit were: chronic viral hepatitis, 33.4% (1749/5240), miscellaneous hepatobiliary conditions including neoplasms, 32.9% (1725/5240) and known/suspected MASLD, 24.7% (1293/5240) (pooled prevalence of 26.1% (95% CI: 19.1-34.7)). 1134 suspected/confirmed MASLD patients were included, the diagnosis was confirmed in 80.2% (909/1134). Significant fibrosis was documented in 22.7% (257/1134) and cirrhosis (including burn-out MASLD) in 21.3% (241/1134). Procedures performed differed between countries, overall 66.4% (753/1134) had imaging studies, 65.3% (740/1134) non-invasive fibrosis tests, 20.4% (231/1134) liver biopsy, while referral for further cardiometabolic assessment or therapy was minimal (144/1134, 15.8%). The cost of all procedures and visits was in the range of that recommended for exploring hepatitis C before treatment, although highly variable between countries. MASLD was the second most frequent single cause for outpatient visits in eight European tertiary care centers. Significant fibrosis including cirrhosis was diagnosed in 44% of patients. The cost of required additional visits and procedures was equivalent to that recommended for hepatitis C before antiviral treatment. IMI2-Grant Agreement 777377-LITMUS.

items.title: FSTL1 high hepatic stellate cells secrete CCL3 to activate the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway, initiating anoikis resistance and promoting hepatocellular carcinoma progression.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) ranks among the most prevalent malignant tumors globally. Approximately 90% of HCC cases arise in the context of liver fibrosis, with hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) playing a pivotal role in the fibrogenic process. Follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL1) is a secreted protein of interest in this study, which examines its impact on liver cancer cells and further elucidates its role in HCC by activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway to induce anoikis resistance. The findings indicate that FSTL1 is predominantly localized in HSCs within HCC tissues and exhibits upregulated expression compared to cirrhotic tissues. Experimental manipulation of FSTL1 expression, through stable overexpression or knockdown, correspondingly enhanced or inhibited the proliferation and migration capabilities of HSCs in vitro. Furthermore, HSCs with high FSTL1 expression were observed to facilitate the migration, invasion, in vivo growth, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) of HCC cells. In particular, HSCs with elevated levels of FSTL1 secrete CCL3, which interacts with the CCR5 receptor on the surface of HCC cells, thereby activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This pathway activation inhibits anoikis in HCC cells, facilitating their migration, invasion, and growth in vivo. In a nude mouse model, HSCs with high FSTL1 expression significantly enhanced the growth of subcutaneous tumors derived from HCC cells. This was demonstrated by an increased Ki-67 positive index, elevated levels of CCL3 and CCR5 expression, increased Bcl-2 expression, and decreased Caspase-3 expression. In summary, HSCs with high FSTL1 expression inhibit anoikis in HCC cells through the CCL3-CCR5-PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis, thereby promoting tumor progression.
items.journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. Molecular basis of disease

items.title: Investigating the Expression and Function of PPP2R1A in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multi-Omics Analysis with in vitro Validation.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains difficult to diagnose early and to treat effectively. Protein Phosphatase 2A Regulatory Subunit Aα ( PPP2R1A ), the scaffolding (Aα) subunit of the PP2A holoenzyme, is altered in several cancer types, but its expression pattern, functional significance, and translational relevance in HCC are incompletely understood. Public transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-LIHC, GTEx, GEO, ICGC-LIHC, HPA, TISCH2) and drug-sensitivity databases were integrated to characterize PPP2R1A expression and its associations with survival, biological pathways, and tumor immune infiltration in HCC. Functional effects of PPP2R1A knockdown were assessed in Huh7 cells by RT-qPCR, CCK-8, Transwell, flow-cytometric cell-cycle, and β-galactosidase assays. PPP2R1A was significantly overexpressed in HCC tissues relative to normal liver and was also elevated across several other cancer types. High PPP2R1A expression was associated with shorter overall and disease-specific survival in Kaplan-Meier analysis, although it was not an independent prognostic factor after multivariate adjustment (hazard ratio [HR] = 1.051, p = 0.789). PPP2R1A expression correlated positively with transcriptional programs related to cell cycle, MYC, EGFR, MAPK, and WNT signaling, and negatively with p53 pathway activity. At single-cell and spatial resolution, PPP2R1A was enriched in malignant cells and in tumor regions, and its expression correlated with the abundance of several computationally inferred immune cell populations. PPP2R1A knockdown in Huh7 cells reduced proliferation and invasion, induced G2-phase arrest, and decreased MYC, CDK1, and CCNB1 mRNA expression without inducing senescence. Drug-sensitivity screens suggested candidate agents, such as AT-7519, that warrant further investigation in PPP2R1A -high HCC. PPP2R1A is consistently overexpressed in HCC and contributes to the malignant phenotype at least partly through cell-cycle regulation. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and the potential diagnostic, prognostic, or therapeutic value of PPP2R1A in HCC requires dedicated prospective and functional validation.

items.title: Outcomes of Patients with Rare Cancers Treated with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors with and Without Lung and/or Liver Metastases (NCI/SWOG S1609).
items.abstract: Limited prior retrospective data, primarily among patients with lung cancer, liver cancer, and melanoma, has indicated that liver metastases are associated with poorer outcomes with chemotherapy, targeted agents, and checkpoint inhibitor therapy. We used a unique clinical trial resource to evaluate whether liver and/or lung metastases were associated with outcomes among patients with rare tumors treated with combination anti-CTLA-4 (cytotoxic T-lymphocyte-associated protein 4) and anti-PD-1 (programmed cell death protein 1) therapy. The basket trial, SWOG trial S1609 (NCT02834013, DART trial), treated 655 eligible patients without lung or liver primary cancers. Associations with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated with Cox regression models. Associations with clinical benefit rate (confirmed complete and partial response or stable disease for 6 months or longer) and treatment-related adverse events (per CTCAEv5) were evaluated using Fisher exact test. There was no significant difference in rates of grade 3 or higher treatment-related adverse events across the groups. Participants with liver metastases, with or without lung metastases, had a lower likelihood of experiencing clinical benefit (11% and 18%, respectively) compared with participants with lung but not liver metastases or participants with neither lung nor liver metastases (26% and 30%, respectively, p = 0.003). On multivariable analysis, having both lung and liver metastases was associated with shorter PFS and OS compared with the presence of neither liver nor lung metastases when accounting for the number of RECIST (Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors) target sites. Compared with the presence of neither liver nor lung metastases, lung but not liver or liver but not lung sites of metastases were significantly associated with PFS but not OS in these multivariable models. In a diverse cohort of participants with advanced rare tumors treated with combination anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-1 therapy, we found that both the combination of lung and liver metastases was associated with shorter PFS and OS.
items.journal: Journal of immunotherapy and precision oncology

items.title: Segmental distribution of hepatic steatosis on opportunistic low-dose computed tomography: a Couinaud-based analysis.
items.abstract: Hepatic steatosis is commonly and incidentally detected on nonenhanced computed tomography (CT) as areas of low attenuation. Hepatic steatosis is recognized as an independent predictor of cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM), underscoring the clinical significance of its detection and characterization. Low-dose CT (LDCT) performed for lung cancer screening offers a unique opportunity for opportunistic evaluation of hepatic steatosis. The objective of this study is to measure CT attenuation across all eight Couinaud liver segments in patients with incidentally detected hepatic steatosis on lung cancer screening LDCT, and to identify clinical correlates of steatosis. This retrospective, single-center study evaluated hepatic steatosis among patients who underwent LDCT for lung cancer screening between 2019 and 2024; patients with steatosis and available 1.5 mm soft-tissue reconstructions comprised the analytic cohort for segmental analysis. Steatosis was defined as mean liver attenuation <40 Hounsfield units (HU) on unenhanced CT. Mean CT attenuation (HU) was measured in each Couinaud segment on soft-tissue 1.5 mm unenhanced reconstructions and normalized to intrathoracic tracheal air to reduce interscan variability related to scanner calibration and acquisition parameters. Segmental differences were assessed by repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey-Kramer post-hoc correction. Associations between mean liver HU and clinical variables [age, gender, coronary artery calcification (CAC) score, body mass index, DM] were evaluated using t-tests, and multivariable linear regression. Among 1,000 patients, steatosis was identified in 79 (7.9%); 68 with available 1.5 mm reconstructions (70.6% male) comprised the analytic cohort. Patients with steatosis were younger (median 61 vs. 63 years, P=0.005) and had higher BMI (mean 32.43 vs. 28.59 kg/m 2 , P=0.01). Mean liver attenuation was -30.9±30.5 HU (range, -109.2 to +27.6 HU). Segmental attenuation ranged from -27.1±30.8 HU in segment 1 (caudate lobe) to -34.0±30.9 HU in segment 7. Repeated-measures ANOVA demonstrated significant segmental variation (P<0.001); segment 1 showed higher attenuation than segments 3, 4A, 4B, 6, 7, and 8 (all Tukey-adjusted P<0.05), indicating relative caudate sparing. Segments 7 and 8 had the lowest attenuation. Within-patient variability was modest (mean standard deviation: 4.91±1.94 HU), though a subset showed substantial heterogeneity. In multivariable linear regression, older age (β=+0.16/year, P=0.001) and female sex (β=+1.51, P=0.03) were independently associated with higher liver attenuation, while DM was associated with lower attenuation (β=-2.44, P=0.001). In this exploratory, single-center study, the mean attenuation of segments 7 and 8 combined correlated strongly with whole-liver attenuation and may represent a practical candidate proxy for opportunistic screening. Validation in a larger study is needed before this two-segment measurement approach is adopted for routine use.
